properties.title: NX-400 Firmware 4.4 Release Notes
properties.summary:
Firmware 4.4 for the NX-400 dual-socket AC charger, focused on connectivity stability and RFID reliability improvements.

Superseded by version 4.5 (see REL-NX400-4.5).
properties.newFeatures: Added support for extended RFID card whitelists (up to 500 local entries) for sites with intermittent backend connectivity.
properties.improvements: Improved Ethernet link recovery time after a DHCP lease renewal failure.
properties.bugFixes: Fixed an issue where the 4G fallback modem would not re-register with the carrier network after a brief signal loss.
properties.upgradeInstructions: Upgrade via USB firmware package. Remote firmware update is not yet supported on this version — see the NX-400 maintenance procedures.

properties.title: NX-400 Firmware 4.8 Release Notes
properties.summary:
Firmware 4.8 delivers a significant OCPP 2.0.1 session-handling overhaul, improving session-resume reliability after transient network drops.

Superseded by version 4.8.1 (see REL-NX400-4.8.1).
properties.newFeatures: Added OCPP 2.0.1 session-resume support, allowing an in-progress charging session to survive a brief backend network interruption without restarting.
properties.improvements: Improved session-token handling for long-duration charging sessions on dual-socket units.
properties.bugFixes: Fixed a rare condition where a completed session's final meter value was not transmitted to Polaris Billing.
properties.knownIssuesText:
Under sustained high session volume on dual-socket units, an intermittent OCPP backend disconnect (error E217) can occur after approximately 72 hours of continuous uptime. This is tracked under Known Issue KI-NX400-004.

Sites with high daily session turnover on both sockets should monitor for E217 and consider a scheduled overnight OCPP reconnect until the fix in firmware 4.8.1 is applied.
properties.upgradeInstructions: Standard USB firmware update procedure. Customers currently on 4.7 or earlier should plan to upgrade directly to 4.8.1 once available to avoid the E217 known issue introduced in this release.

properties.title: NX-400 Firmware 4.5 Release Notes
properties.summary:
Firmware 4.5 adds dynamic load balancing refinements and addresses a circuit-breaker false-trip issue reported on some dual-socket sites.

Superseded by version 4.6 (see REL-NX400-4.6).
properties.newFeatures: Introduced configurable load-balancing headroom margin, letting installers reserve extra circuit capacity for future expansion.
properties.improvements: Reduced dynamic load-balancing recalculation latency between the two sockets from ~2s to under 500ms.
properties.bugFixes: Fixed a rare false-positive overcurrent trip (E301) observed when both sockets ramped up simultaneously from an idle state.
properties.upgradeInstructions: Standard USB firmware update procedure.

properties.title: NX-400 Firmware 4.6 Release Notes
properties.summary:
Firmware 4.6 improves Polaris backend heartbeat resilience and refines meter synchronization accuracy for billing.

Superseded by version 4.7 (see REL-NX400-4.7).
properties.newFeatures: Added configurable heartbeat interval to Polaris Charge Cloud, reducing false E101 offline alerts on high-latency cellular links.
properties.improvements: Improved meter reading precision reported to Polaris Billing, reducing E404 meter-sync mismatches.
properties.bugFixes: Fixed an issue where a charging session could remain open in Polaris after a local power interruption ended the session on the unit.
properties.upgradeInstructions: Standard USB firmware update procedure.

properties.title: NX-400 Firmware 4.7 Release Notes
properties.summary:
Firmware 4.7 is a maintenance release preparing the OCPP 2.0.1 stack for the upcoming 4.8 session-handling overhaul, plus general stability fixes.

Superseded by version 4.8 (see REL-NX400-4.8).
properties.improvements: Internal refactor of the OCPP 2.0.1 message queue to reduce memory fragmentation during long-running sessions.
properties.bugFixes: Fixed an intermittent RFID reader timeout (E117) that could occur immediately after a firmware update reboot.
properties.upgradeInstructions: Standard USB firmware update procedure. Remote update via Polaris remains unsupported on NX-400 through this version.

properties.title: NX-400 Firmware 4.8.1 Release Notes
properties.summary: Firmware 4.8.1 is a targeted patch release that fixes the OCPP backend disconnect issue (error E217) introduced in firmware 4.8, and resolves Known Issue KI-NX400-004.
properties.improvements: Minor logging improvements to the OCPP client to aid future diagnostics of long-uptime connection issues.
properties.bugFixes:
Fixes error E217 (intermittent OCPP backend disconnect after ~72 hours of continuous uptime on dual-socket units under high session volume). Root cause: a session-token cache leak in the OCPP client that accumulated stale entries over long uptime periods, eventually exhausting available memory for new sessions and forcing a backend disconnect. Fixed by correcting the cache eviction logic to properly expire stale session tokens.

This release resolves Known Issue KI-NX400-004 in full — no workaround is required after upgrading.
properties.upgradeInstructions: All NX-400 units running firmware 4.8 should be upgraded to 4.8.1 as soon as possible via USB or the scheduled maintenance window. Units on 4.7 or earlier can upgrade directly to 4.8.1.
properties.tags: firmware, NX-400, OCPP, bugfix, E217, KI-NX400-004

properties.title: NX-450 Firmware 1.0 Release Notes
properties.summary:
Firmware 1.0 is the launch release for the NX-450, the premium successor to the NX-400. It introduces Plug & Charge support and improved energy metering, in addition to the full NX-400 feature set (OCPP 2.0.1, dynamic load balancing, RFID, integrated 4G).

Superseded by version 1.1 (see REL-NX450-1.1).
properties.newFeatures:
Introduces Plug & Charge (ISO 15118) support, allowing an enrolled vehicle to authenticate and start a charging session automatically without an RFID card or app interaction.

Improved energy-metering accuracy compared to the NX-400 platform, supporting tighter billing reconciliation with Polaris.
properties.breakingChanges: The NX-450 is a new hardware platform and is not a firmware upgrade path for existing NX-400 units. NX-400 firmware releases and NX-450 firmware releases are independent version sequences.
properties.upgradeInstructions: Initial release — shipped pre-installed on new NX-450 units. Remote firmware updates via Polaris are supported from this version onward.

properties.title: NX-450 Firmware 1.1 Release Notes
properties.summary:
Firmware 1.1 fixes a Plug & Charge certificate-renewal issue that could cause automatic authentication to silently stop working after the initial contract certificate expired.

Superseded by version 1.2 (see REL-NX450-1.2).
properties.improvements: Improved Plug & Charge contract-certificate renewal handling ahead of expiry, reducing the chance of an authentication failure at the charger.
properties.bugFixes: Fixed an issue where a Plug & Charge contract certificate nearing expiry was not renewed automatically in time, causing the vehicle to fall back to manual RFID/app authentication without a clear on-unit indication.
properties.upgradeInstructions: Remote firmware update via Polaris is supported and preferred for this release. USB update remains available as a fallback.

properties.title: NX-450 Firmware 1.2 Release Notes
properties.summary: Firmware 1.2 improves energy-metering accuracy further, refining the billing data reported to Polaris Charge Cloud.
properties.improvements: Improved energy-metering accuracy under variable load conditions (e.g. dynamic load balancing actively throttling one socket), reducing small billing discrepancies previously seen on mixed-load sessions.
properties.bugFixes: Fixed a minor rounding inconsistency in the kWh value reported for very short charging sessions (under 2 minutes).
properties.upgradeInstructions: Remote firmware update via Polaris is supported and preferred for this release.

properties.title: Polaris Charge Cloud 2024.1 Release Notes
properties.summary:
Polaris Charge Cloud 2024.1 delivers general platform stability improvements across Device Management, Driver Management, Billing, and Monitoring.

Superseded by version 2024.3 (see REL-POLARIS-2024.3).
properties.improvements:
Improved dashboard load time for accounts managing more than 200 charging stations.

Refined Monitoring module alert thresholds to reduce noisy E101 offline notifications during brief network blips.
properties.bugFixes: Fixed an issue in Driver Management where a deactivated RFID card could remain listed as active for up to 24 hours.
properties.upgradeInstructions: SaaS release — applied automatically to all Polaris Charge Cloud tenants. No customer action required.

properties.title: Polaris Charge Cloud 2024.3 Release Notes
properties.summary:
Polaris Charge Cloud 2024.3 introduces the Remote Diagnostics module, enabling support engineers to pull live diagnostic snapshots from a charging station without an on-site visit.

Superseded by version 2025.1 (see REL-POLARIS-2025.1).
properties.newFeatures: Added the Remote Diagnostics module, allowing authorized support agents to request a live diagnostic snapshot (connectivity status, recent error codes, firmware version) from any connected unit directly from the Polaris console.
properties.improvements: Improved Billing module reconciliation reporting for multi-site accounts.
properties.bugFixes: Fixed an occasional duplicate session entry in Reporting for sessions that resumed after a brief OCPP reconnect.
properties.upgradeInstructions: SaaS release — applied automatically. Remote Diagnostics requires the requesting user account to hold the Support Agent role in Polaris.

properties.title: Polaris Charge Cloud 2025.1 Release Notes
properties.summary:
Polaris Charge Cloud 2025.1 introduces the API Management module and adds OAuth2 client-credentials support for programmatic integrations.

Superseded by version 2025.4 (see REL-POLARIS-2025.4).
properties.newFeatures:
Added the API Management module, giving administrators a self-service console to issue and revoke API credentials.

Added OAuth2 client-credentials grant support for machine-to-machine integrations, alongside the existing user-delegated authentication flows.
properties.improvements: Improved API rate-limit visibility, surfacing current usage against plan limits directly in the API Management console.
properties.bugFixes: Fixed an issue where an expired API token returned a generic 500 error instead of a clear 401 Unauthorized response.
properties.breakingChanges: Existing integrations using the legacy static API key mechanism continue to work, but static keys are deprecated in favor of OAuth2 client credentials and will be phased out in a future release — see the API Management documentation for migration guidance.
properties.upgradeInstructions: SaaS release — applied automatically. Existing integrations are unaffected until static API keys are formally deprecated.

properties.title: Polaris Charge Cloud 2025.4 Release Notes
properties.summary: Polaris Charge Cloud 2025.4 adds mid-session tariff-change support to the Billing module, allowing a time-of-use tariff change to apply correctly to a session already in progress.
properties.newFeatures: Added mid-session tariff-change support to Billing, so a charging session spanning a time-of-use tariff boundary (e.g. peak to off-peak) is now billed in segments at the correct rate for each period instead of a single flat rate for the whole session.
properties.improvements: Improved Billing module invoice line-item detail to show the tariff segments applied to a multi-rate session.
properties.bugFixes: Fixed an E404 meter-sync mismatch that could occur on sessions crossing a tariff boundary under the previous single-rate billing logic.
properties.upgradeInstructions: SaaS release — applied automatically. Accounts using time-of-use tariffs should review recent invoices after this release to confirm the new segmented billing behavior matches expectations.

properties.title: Orion Energy Manager 3.0 Release Notes
properties.summary:
Orion Energy Manager 3.0 is the initial general-availability release, providing building load balancing, charging priority rules, and peak demand management.

Superseded by version 3.1 (see REL-ORION-3.1).
properties.newFeatures:
Initial GA release of Orion Energy Manager.

Building-wide load balancing across all connected Nova AC/DC charging stations on a site.

Configurable charging priority rules, including the ability to prioritize company/fleet vehicles over visitor vehicles.

Peak demand management to keep total site load under a configured demand charge threshold.
properties.upgradeInstructions: Initial release — no upgrade path applicable.

properties.title: Orion Energy Manager 3.1 Release Notes
properties.summary:
Orion Energy Manager 3.1 adds solar-generation-aware priority rules, letting on-site solar output influence charging priority decisions.

Superseded by version 3.2 (see REL-ORION-3.2).
properties.newFeatures: Added solar-generation-aware priority rules — Orion can now factor real-time on-site solar generation into charging priority decisions, favoring charging sessions when excess solar output is available.
properties.improvements: Improved peak demand management responsiveness when solar generation drops suddenly (e.g. cloud cover).
properties.bugFixes: Fixed a case where a manually overridden priority rule was not correctly restored after a scheduled rule window ended.
properties.upgradeInstructions: Standard platform update, applied per deployment schedule. Solar-generation-aware rules require an on-site solar meter integration to be configured.

properties.title: Orion Energy Manager 3.2 Release Notes
properties.summary: Orion Energy Manager 3.2 adds battery storage integration, allowing on-site battery systems to participate in load balancing and peak demand management alongside solar and grid supply.
properties.newFeatures: Added battery storage integration — Orion can now dispatch on-site battery storage to supplement charging load during peak demand periods, and factor battery state of charge into charging priority decisions.
properties.improvements: Improved coordination between solar-generation-aware priority rules (from 3.1) and the new battery dispatch logic to avoid conflicting charge/discharge decisions.
properties.bugFixes: Fixed an edge case where peak demand management could briefly exceed the configured threshold during a rapid load ramp-up across multiple chargers.
properties.upgradeInstructions: Standard platform update. Battery storage integration requires a supported battery system connector to be configured before the new dispatch features become active.

properties.title: Atlas Fleet 2.0 Release Notes
properties.summary:
Atlas Fleet 2.0 delivers core fleet management and EV charging optimization capabilities for corporate and logistics fleets.

Superseded by version 2.1 (see REL-ATLAS-2.1).
properties.newFeatures: Core fleet vehicle roster management, charging schedule optimization across a fleet's assigned charging stations, and integration with Polaris Charge Cloud for session data.
properties.upgradeInstructions: Initial major release in this version sequence — no upgrade path applicable.

properties.title: Atlas Fleet 2.1 Release Notes
properties.summary:
Atlas Fleet 2.1 adds route-aware charge scheduling, factoring a vehicle's planned route into charging schedule optimization.

Superseded by version 2.2 (see REL-ATLAS-2.2).
properties.newFeatures: Added route-aware charge scheduling — Atlas now factors a vehicle's next planned route (distance, expected departure time) into its charging schedule, prioritizing vehicles with an earlier or longer route ahead of others with more charging headroom.
properties.improvements: Improved charging schedule optimization to better balance fleet-wide charger availability during shift changes.
properties.bugFixes: Fixed an issue where a vehicle removed from the fleet roster mid-session could leave a stale scheduling entry.
properties.upgradeInstructions: Standard platform update. Route-aware scheduling requires route data to be provided via the fleet's routing integration.

properties.title: Atlas Fleet 2.2 Release Notes
properties.summary:
Atlas Fleet 2.2 adds depot capacity forecasting, helping fleet operators anticipate charging capacity needs as the fleet grows.

Superseded by version 2.3 (see REL-ATLAS-2.3).
properties.newFeatures: Added depot capacity forecasting — Atlas projects future charging capacity needs at a depot based on historical usage trends and planned fleet growth, flagging depots likely to need additional charging stations.
properties.improvements: Improved route-aware charge scheduling (introduced in 2.1) to account for multi-stop routes, not just a single next destination.
properties.bugFixes: Fixed a reporting discrepancy where depot-level energy consumption totals could undercount sessions split across a midnight boundary.
properties.upgradeInstructions: Standard platform update. Depot capacity forecasting requires at least 3 months of historical usage data to produce a meaningful forecast.

properties.title: Atlas Fleet 2.3 Release Notes
properties.summary: Atlas Fleet 2.3 ships driver mobile app v2, a redesigned mobile experience for fleet drivers to locate, reserve, and start charging sessions.
properties.newFeatures: Released driver mobile app v2 — a redesigned mobile app for fleet drivers, including charger reservation, real-time charger availability across the fleet's depots, and push notifications when a reserved charger becomes free.
properties.improvements: Improved depot capacity forecasting (from 2.2) accuracy by incorporating reservation data from the new mobile app.
properties.bugFixes: Fixed several stability issues in the legacy driver app that are resolved by migrating to app v2.
properties.breakingChanges: The legacy driver mobile app (v1) is deprecated as of this release and will no longer receive updates. Fleet administrators should plan driver migration to app v2.
properties.upgradeInstructions: Standard platform update for the Atlas backend. Drivers must separately update to driver mobile app v2 from their device's app store.
